li.label: more bandage lessons
li.description: Every afternoon another lesson in tying bandages. I have real work to do.

li.label: first-aid lessons
li.description: An hour a day learning to bind wounds. I'd rather leave it to the doctor.

li.label: first-aid lessons
li.description: I know how to stop a wound bleeding now. That could matter one day.

li.label: teaching first aid
li.description: Everyone here can bind a wound now, and I helped teach them.

li.label: animals all day
li.description: Every day out at the pens with the animals. I'm not a herder.

li.label: days with the animals
li.description: An hour at the pens every day, whether I'm any good with them or not.

li.label: days with the animals
li.description: The animals are calmer with us now, and so am I.

li.label: days with the animals
li.description: The council gave us whole days with the animals. I couldn't ask for better.

li.label: stuck at the bench
li.description: Day after day indoors at the bench while the work outside waits.

li.label: bench work
li.description: Everyone at the benches. I'd rather be outside, even in the cold.

li.label: work at the benches
li.description: A warm room and something good taking shape on the bench. That's how to spend the cold months.

li.label: work at the benches
li.description: Long days at the bench with the stove going. This is my favourite time of year.

li.label: our medicine given away
li.description: Our medicine goes out of the gate every morning, and one day we'll need it ourselves.

li.label: medicine sent away
li.description: We're sending medicine to strangers while our own shelves get thin.

li.label: medicine for the sick
li.description: Our medicine is helping the sick down the road. That's a good use for it.

li.label: medicine for the sick
li.description: People are getting better because of what we send them every morning.

li.label: our wood given away
li.description: We cut that wood ourselves, and now it goes out of the gate every morning.

li.label: wood sent away
li.description: Our woodpile gets smaller every day so somebody else can stay warm.

li.label: wood for the neighbours
li.description: The neighbours have a hard time of it, and our wood is helping.

li.label: wood for the neighbours
li.description: Our wood is going into their new roofs and their stoves. I'm glad we're doing this.

li.label: mending again
li.description: Every morning, mending something. It'll only get broken again.

li.label: mending days
li.description: Mornings spent patching walls when there's other work to do.

li.label: mending days
li.description: The walls and doors are whole again. It feels safer.

li.label: mending days
li.description: A morning's mending, and everything stands straight again. I like putting things right.

li.label: fishing every day
li.description: Two of us sitting by the water every morning while the real work waits.

li.label: a fishing season
li.description: Fish for supper again. I'd rather the hands were in the fields.

li.label: a fishing season
li.description: Fresh fish every day, and someone always has a story about the one that got away.

li.label: a fishing season
li.description: Mornings by the water with a line out. The council got this one right.
